fields.System.Title: RET-4 — Disposition
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Send inspected stock to the right destination — back to sale, to repair, to the supplier, or to
scrap.

Scope

In. The five disposition paths and the ERP credit notification.

Out. Repair execution. Refund payment.

Design notes

Restocked stock gets a fresh receipt date and re-captured expiry. A unit that spent three
months on a customer's shelf is not as good as new. Reusing the original batch's dates makes
FEFO treat old stock as fresh, and can make already-expired stock sellable again.

Scrap is a movement to VIRT-LOSS with approval and a reason code. It destroys stock by
hand, so it gets the same controls as an adjustment.

Sequence the ERP credit after disposition, not after receipt. Crediting on arrival means
refunding for goods that turn out to be scrap, or worse, for goods that were never sold.

Graded stock needs its own location and its own availability treatment — it is sellable,
but not as the same product at the same price. Keep it physically and logically separate from
new stock.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Restocked with the original expiry | [doc 09 §8.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Damaged stock restocked as new | [doc 09 §8.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Credit raised before inspection | [doc 05 WF 9](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Graded stock mixed with new stock | [doc 05 WF 9](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
